answer: One concrete anti-Sybil mechanism requires each agent to harbor a unique hardware security module that cryptographically binds its identity to a physical chip. An attacker must purchase and provision a separate module for every fake identity, so the marginal cost scales linearly and cannot be amortized across many sybils. This creates a river of real-world expense that grows with each additional identity, rendering mass attacks uneconomical even when software is free. A violet status LED on the module can further confirm physical presence during initial registration.
